/en-in/attractions/ancient-city-muang-bo: Muang Boran Ancient City timings and entry fee: open 09:00–19:00, 800 baht for foreign adults and 400 baht for kids aged 6–14. Car entry costs extra, separate from golf cart rental inside the park.
/en-in/attractions/aquaria-phuket/: Aquaria Phuket ticket price and timings: the official online aquarium-only ticket is 1,251 baht for adults, open 11:00–19:00 at Central Phuket Floresta. Not the same as Phuket Aquarium at Cape Panwa.
/en-in/attractions/ayutthaya-historical-: Ayutthaya temples worth seeing: Wat Mahathat’s Buddha head in tree roots, the three chedis of Wat Phra Si Sanphet and riverside Wat Chaiwatthanaram. Ruins are spread out; entry is paid site by site.
/en-in/attractions/bangsaen-aquarium/: Bangsaen Aquarium timings in Chonburi: 09:00–16:00, closed Monday. Catch diver feeding at 14:30 (plus 10:30 on weekends), touch-pool sessions and Big Tank feeding, and read species labels with kids.
/en-in/attractions/bophut-fishermans-vil: Fisherman’s Village Koh Samui shopping guide: walk the Bophut coast road for hand-carved soap, wooden crafts, jewellery and clothes, then eat seafood facing the sea at dinner time.
/en-in/attractions/bridge-over-river-kwa: River Kwai Bridge Kanchanaburi guide: see the steel bridge of the Thailand–Burma Railway, repaired in 1946 after wartime bombing, from the riverbank or by train, following staff rules.
/en-in/attractions/bueng-boraphet-aquari: Bueng Boraphet Aquarium Nakhon Sawan: walk through the 24-metre freshwater tunnel, then see 33+ tanks with sea and non-local species. The lake, visitor centre and aquarium keep separate hours.
/en-in/attractions/bueng-chawak-aquarium: Bueng Chawak Aquarium timings: weekdays 08:30–16:30, weekends till 17:00. Check if your ticket covers Building 2’s freshwater tunnel, Building 3’s shark tank, or both, plus the tiger and lion areas.
/en-in/attractions/categories/markets/: Best markets in Thailand for shopping and street food: compare 12 picks by city, including Chatuchak weekend market, Mae Klong Railway Market, Chiang Mai Night Bazaar and Cicada Market in Hua Hin.
/en-in/attractions/categories/temples/: Famous temples in Thailand to add to your trip: filter 30 picks by city, from Wat Arun and the Emerald Buddha in Bangkok to Doi Suthep, Chiang Rai’s Blue Temple and the Big Buddha on Samui.
/en-in/attractions/categories/theme-wate: Water parks in Thailand for a family day out: Andamanda in Phuket, Ramayana south of Pattaya, Vana Nava in Hua Hin and Siam Amazing Park in Bangkok, with Dream World’s Snow Town and ride rules.
/en-in/attractions/charoen-krung/: Charoen Krung Bangkok things to do: see the Grand Postal Building housing TCDC, then browse clothes, homeware, flowers and records at Warehouse 30. Map the building you want, not the road.
/en-in/attractions/chatuchak-market/: Chatuchak weekend market timings and how to reach: weekends 09:00–18:00, plants Thursday–Friday from 07:00, Friday night shops 18:00–24:00. Nearest stops are MRT Chatuchak Park and BTS Mo Chit.
/en-in/attractions/chiang-mai-night-baza: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar shopping and timings: open every evening roughly 16:00–23:30 along Chang Khlan Road. Buy crafts and souvenirs, then eat at the Anusarn Market food area nearby.
/en-in/attractions/chiang-mai-night-safa: Chiang Mai Night Safari tickets and routes: see giraffes and zebras on Savanna Safari and tigers and lions on Predator Prowl by vehicle, then the walking exhibits and shows in your booking.
/en-in/attractions/chiang-mai-zoo/: Chiang Mai Zoo ticket price: 350 baht for adults, 120 baht for kids under 135 cm, golf cart 350 baht an hour for elders or long walks. The aquarium is extra and the Night Safari is a separate venue.
/en-in/attractions/damnoen-saduak-floati: Damnoen Saduak floating market day trip from Bangkok: about two hours away, with tours leaving around 06:30–07:00 to see morning boats selling fruit and noodles along Khlong Ton Khem in Ratchaburi.
/en-in/attractions/erawan-museum/: Erawan Museum ticket price and timings: adults 500 baht, children 250 baht, open 09:00–18:00 with the ticket office closing at 17:00. Audio guides in English; garden with mythical animal statues.
/en-in/attractions/jim-thompson-house/: Jim Thompson House Bangkok entry fee: 250 baht for adults, 150 baht for ages 10–21 with ID, free under 10. A guide is required in the main house; walk from Exit 1 of National Stadium BTS.
/en-in/attractions/khao-kheow-open-zoo/: Khao Kheow Open Zoo ticket price and show timings: adults 350 baht, children 120 baht, open 08:00–17:00. See Moo Deng, plus the weekday and weekend schedule for elephant and penguin programmes.
/en-in/attractions/khao-san-road/: Khao San Road nightlife and stay guide: Bangkok’s backpacker street has dorms to hotel rooms, pubs, clubs and food from pad Thai to pizza. Check air conditioning and night-time noise before booking.
/en-in/attractions/khlong-lat-mayom-floa: Khlong Lat Mayom floating market food guide: try som tam, grilled chicken, boat noodles and khanom ko, plus pomelo and coconuts, then shop for straw hats and herbal products. Open weekends.
/en-in/attractions/mae-klong-railway-mar: How to reach Mae Klong Railway Market from Bangkok by train: Wongwian Yai to Mahachai, ferry across the river, then Ban Laem to Mae Klong. Check train arrival times to watch stalls fold away.
/en-in/attractions/museum-siam/: Museum Siam Bangkok timings and ticket: 10:00–18:00, closed Monday, entry 100 baht. A good indoor stop after the Grand Palace, with interactive games and parking free for three hours with a receipt.
/en-in/attractions/nakhon-ratchasima-zoo: Korat Zoo ticket price and getting around: foreign adults 350 baht, children 120 baht. Inside, use the shuttle at 15–30 baht a ride, golf carts from 300 baht an hour or bicycles from 20 baht.
/en-in/attractions/national-museum-bangk: National Museum Bangkok entry fee and timings: 240 baht, closes at 16:00, shut on Monday, Tuesday and public holidays. Free volunteer guided tours start at 09:30 from the ticket office.
/en-in/attractions/nimmanhaemin/: Nimman Road Chiang Mai cafes and shopping: browse scented candles and embroidered bags on Soi 1, an artist’s gallery cafe on Soi 17 and One Nimman, about 15 minutes from the city centre by songthaew.
/en-in/attractions/nong-khai-aquarium/: Nong Khai Aquarium visit: walk down the 34-metre tunnel from sea fish to Mekong River fish in nine exhibit groups. It is in Nong Kom Ko, Nong Khai, not Khon Kaen city; contact 042-415-623.
/en-in/attractions/phuket-aquarium/: Phuket Aquarium Cape Panwa timings: 08:30–16:30, ticket office closes at 16:00. Watch diver feeding at 11:00 and an animated film every 30 minutes. Not the same as Aquaria Phuket in the mall.
/en-in/attractions/phuket-old-town/: Phuket Old Town things to do: walk Thalang Road’s colourful shophouses, spot street art, learn Chinese community history at Thai Hua Museum and visit Lard Yai market, held on Sunday evenings.
/en-in/attractions/safari-world/: Safari World Bangkok timings and shows: open Tuesday to Sunday, Safari Park from 09:00 by own car or park coach, Marine Park until 17:30 on weekends. Plan dolphin shows by weekday schedule.
/en-in/attractions/sea-life-bangkok/: SEA LIFE Bangkok tickets and feeding times: open 10:00–20:00 at Siam Paragon, last entry 19:00. Watch feeding sessions free with admission and walk over sharks on the glass floor of Shark Walk.
/en-in/attractions/taling-chan-floating-: Taling Chan floating market food guide: sit on a raft by the canal for seafood, boat noodles and som tam, then book a canal boat tour separately. Not to be confused with Khlong Lat Mayom.
/en-in/attractions/waghor-aquarium/: Waghor Aquarium Prachuap Khiri Khan for students and families: six zones from freshwater to sea, a glass tunnel and dolphin and dugong models. School groups must apply two weeks ahead for a briefing.
/en-in/attractions/wat-arun/: Wat Arun timings, ticket price and how to reach: 08:00–18:00, 200 baht for foreigners. Walk from Itsaraphap MRT, take a boat to Wat Arun Pier, or cross by ferry from Tha Tien on the Wat Pho side.
/en-in/attractions/wat-pho/: Wat Pho Bangkok timings and ticket price: 08:30–20:00, last entry 19:30, entry 300 baht. Walk five minutes from Sanam Chai MRT or come by boat to Tha Tien to see the giant Reclining Buddha.
/en-in/attractions/wat-phra-kaew/: Emerald Buddha temple Bangkok entry: no separate ticket, as it comes with the Grand Palace pass of 500 baht, free for kids under 120 cm. Tickets sold 08:30–15:30 or online up to a month ahead.
/en-in/attractions/wat-phra-mahathat-nak: Wat Phra Mahathat Nakhon Si Thammarat guide: a key Buddhist centre of the south where you can walk around the relic chedi, learn about the cloth-wrapping ceremony and Nora dance-drama traditions.
/en-in/attractions/wat-phra-si-sanphet/: Three chedis of Ayutthaya at Wat Phra Si Sanphet: learn which kings rest in each tower, how a royal palace became a ceremonial temple, and trace the remaining hall foundations on your visit.
/en-in/attractions/wat-phra-singh/: Wat Phra Singh Chiang Mai timings and entry: 07:00–22:00, 50 baht. Pay respects at the Phra Singh Buddha, compare the Suwannahong and Golden Conch murals, then see the golden chedi outside.
/en-in/attractions/wat-phra-yai-samui/: Big Buddha temple Samui guide: cross the causeway to Koh Fan to see the golden Phra Phuttha Kodom in earth-witness posture, a working place of worship, not to be confused with Phuket’s Big Buddha.
/en-in/attractions/wat-plai-laem/: Wat Plai Laem Samui: see the many-armed white Guanyin statue rising from a pond, cross the marble bridge to the hall by the water, and allow separate time for the nearby Big Buddha temple.
/en-in/attractions/wat-rong-khun/: White Temple Chiang Rai timings and ticket: 08:00–17:00, entry 200 baht. It is about 14 km from Chiang Rai town, so plan travel time to see the bridge, white hall and fine sculptures.
/en-in/attractions/wat-rong-suea-ten/: Blue Temple Chiang Rai entry and timings: free, open 07:00–20:00 in Rim Kok, about 4 km from town towards the airport. Study the coiled naga sculpture and blue details around the hall.
/en-in/attractions/wat-si-chum-sukhothai: Wat Si Chum Sukhothai guide: glimpse the giant Phra Achana Buddha through a narrow gap, then look up inside. Tickets are sold by zone, so travel separately from the central walled zone.
/en-in/attractions/wat-suthat/: Wat Suthat and Giant Swing timings: temple 08:30–20:00 at 100 baht; the museum opens only Friday to Sunday and holidays, 09:30–16:00, for 200 baht. About 10 minutes on foot from Sam Yot MRT.
/en-in/attractions/wat-yai-chai-mongkhon: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon Ayutthaya entry fee and timings: 40 baht, 08:00–17:00. See the tall chedi with corner towers, the Reclining Buddha, and learn its link to monks trained in Sri Lanka.
/en-in/attractions/wualai-saturday-marke: Chiang Mai Saturday Walking Street on Wualai Road: shop silver jewellery and woven textiles, then eat grilled fish or pad Thai. Stalls open on Saturday evenings; silver shops trade on weekdays.
/en-in/attractions/yaowarat-chinatown/: Bangkok Chinatown Yaowarat things to do: see gold jewellery shops and old shophouses, visit Mahayana and Taoist shrines in the lanes, and shop clothes, shoes and toys wholesale on Vanich Road.
/en-in/beaches/chaweng/: Chaweng Beach Koh Samui for couples and families: walk the long white sand near your hotel and relax by the sea. Give the hotel name to your driver so you do not end up at Chaweng Noi instead.
/en-in/beaches/cities/ko-chang/: Best beaches in Koh Chang for a family stay: pick White Sand Beach for nearby food and shops, or quieter, palm-lined Klong Prao on the west coast. See both on the map with access tips.
/en-in/beaches/cities/pattaya/: Pattaya beach or Jomtien beach? Compare the busy bay on Beach Road near shopping and food with the long, relaxed seafront to the south, and note that Jomtien Bus Terminal is not on the beach.
/en-in/beaches/cities/phuket/: Best beaches in Phuket for your trip: Patong for food and shopping after a beach walk, Karon Yai for a long quiet stroll, Kata Yai for a curved bay. All west coast beaches reached by road.
/en-in/beaches/hua-hin/: Hua Hin beach horse riding and family walks: ask if rides are operating and agree the price first, watch for passing horses, and plan a separate trip south to Khao Takiab’s beach and hilltop temple.
/en-in/beaches/jomtien/: Jomtien Beach Pattaya for a relaxed family day: walk the long sand near your hotel and eat by the coast road. Swim only in permitted areas away from water sports gear, and never under a red flag.
/en-in/beaches/karon/: Karon Beach Phuket for couples and families: a long, open white beach for slow walks and nearby meals. Karon and Kata are separate beaches, and on high-wave or red-flag days keep to the shore.
/en-in/beaches/kata/: Kata Beach Phuket guide: relax on the curved bay, then eat and shop around Kata Yai. Tell your driver Kata or Kata Noi clearly, swim away from surfing areas and plan travel time if adding Karon.
/en-in/beaches/klong-prao/: Klong Prao Koh Chang for couples and families: walk the wide palm-lined sand and eat nearby. With luggage, ask your hotel whether vehicles reach the door, and never swim at Laem Chai Chet cape.
/en-in/beaches/lamai/: Is Lamai Beach Samui safe for kids? Some sections have deep water and strong waves, so keep children close. Enjoy a walk along the palm-lined sand and a meal nearby; travel from Chaweng by road.
/en-in/beaches/patong/: Patong Beach Phuket for friends and couples: walk the busy bay, then shop and eat just behind the sand. No boat needed to get there; swim only in permitted zones away from boats and water sports.
/en-in/beaches/wong-duean/: Wong Duean beach Koh Samet guide: book a boat from Ban Phe and confirm whether it lands at Ao Wong Duean or Na Dan Pier, plan your luggage route to the hotel, and relax on the crescent bay.
/en-in/cameras/chaam-thew-talay/: Cha-am live webcam near Thew Talay, shared as CCTV-style photos updated every few minutes by Mike Newman. Compare each image’s time stamp to see how the local sky and scenery change through the day.
/en-in/cameras/chainat-chao-phraya/: Chao Phraya dam Chai Nat live cam: a CCTV view of the river and dam surroundings listed on Webcamera24. Useful if you want inland river scenery in Thailand instead of the sea.
/en-in/cameras/chiangmai-weather-view/: Chiang Mai weather live cam: pick a CCTV camera or photo feed from EaseWeather and Windy listings to check the city sky before your trip. Images refresh periodically and show their capture time.
/en-in/cameras/chiangrai-mae-yao/: Chiang Rai Ban Mae Yao live webcam: a CCTV view of northern mountains and temples listed on Webcamera 24. Use it for a scenery preview; it does not confirm the exact location of any one temple.
/en-in/cameras/chiangrai-wat-thep/: Wat Thep Bun Yuen live webcam in Chiang Rai: a CCTV outlook over the temple and northern hills, linked from Webcamera24. Treat it as a scenery preview, not a guide to temple entry points.
/en-in/cameras/huahin-centara/: Centara Grand Hua Hin live webcam: watch the beach and sea in front of the resort on this page’s CCTV-style YouTube player before a family seaside holiday, with a second beach view from KBA.
/en-in/cameras/huahin-kba/: Hua Hin beach live webcam by Kiteboarding Asia: a CCTV-style view of the sea and sky for kitesurfing fans. For actual lessons, follow the school’s schedule and local instructions, not the camera.
/en-in/cameras/krabi-ao-nang-coast/: Ao Nang Krabi live webcam: a GISTDA CCTV view of coastal water and sky off the beach where island and Railay boats start. For boat trips, check operator updates and local weather advice too.
/en-in/cameras/lanta-hat-lant/: Koh Lanta live webcam, introduced as Hat Lant: open this CCTV sea view on Webcamera24 to preview the island’s scenery before you travel. The precise filming beach has not been confirmed.
/en-in/cameras/nakhon-cha-uat/: Cha-uat River live webcam in Nakhon Si Thammarat: a CCTV view of the river surroundings for travellers curious about inland southern Thailand rather than beaches. The video opens on Webcamera24.
/en-in/cameras/pathum-chao-phraya/: Chao Phraya River live webcam in Pathum Thani: see the riverside town and nearby buildings through a CCTV listing gathered by Tufaq, a camera guide covering many regions of Thailand.
/en-in/cameras/pattaya-beach-panorama/: Pattaya beach live webcam panorama: a SkylineWebcams CCTV view of the long seafront and Gulf of Thailand to help you picture the beach city before your Pattaya trip. Opens on the provider’s site.
/en-in/cameras/phangan-sanskara/: Haad Rin beach live webcam, Koh Phangan: watch waves roll in on this CCTV-style YouTube stream from House of Sanskara and preview the seafront and sky before your island holiday.
/en-in/cameras/phuket-cape-panwa/: Cape Panwa live webcam in Phuket: a CCTV-style YouTube feed from a freediving school shows the bay, open sea and sky by day and night. Remember this bay’s conditions are not island-wide.
/en-in/cameras/phuket-karon-marina/: Karon beach live webcam Phuket: see the sea and waves at the southern end of the beach through Marina Phuket Resort’s CCTV view, handy for comparing with Patong and Kata before booking.
/en-in/cameras/phuket-kata-surf/: Kata Beach live webcam for surf and waves: periodically refreshed CCTV-style photos by SSS Phuket via Webcamtaxi. Compare waves and sky in each shot, but follow local flags before swimming.
/en-in/cameras/phuket-patong-panorama/: Patong live webcam panorama, Phuket: see hotels, greenery and the bay in one CCTV frame to picture a holiday mixing beach time, shopping and nightlife before you book your stay.
/en-in/cameras/phuket-patong-tower/: Patong Beach live webcam from the 15th floor of Patong Tower: a CCTV panorama of the sand, Andaman Sea and sunset sky over Phuket’s curved bay, useful for comparing day and evening views.
/en-in/cameras/samet-cocoon/: Na Dan Pier Koh Samet live webcam: a CCTV view of the water and sky from the island towards the mainland, shared by The Cocoon Hostel. Read the actual ferry information separately before you travel.
/en-in/cameras/samui-bang-rak/: Bang Rak beach live webcam, north Samui: a SkylineWebcams CCTV view along the shoreline and sea, opened on the provider’s page. Compare beach names and locations before you pick a Samui hotel.
/en-in/cameras/samui-banyan-tree/: Banyan Tree Samui live webcam: look down from the hillside resort over the bay and beach in one CCTV frame, a handy way to see the overall coastline before a Samui holiday.
/en-in/cameras/samui-baobab/: Lamai beach live webcam Samui, in front of Baobab: a seafront CCTV view of the sand, waves and coconut-lined bay at eye level. Switch to the Black Pearl camera for another angle on Lamai.
/en-in/cameras/samui-black-pearl/: Black Pearl Lamai live webcam: watch the sea and waves on Lamai Beach, Koh Samui, through a CCTV-style YouTube player. It faces seawards, much like the view you would get standing on the sand.
/en-in/cameras/samui-bophut-beach/: Bophut beach live webcam, north Samui: see the shoreline and water in front of Bophut through a SkylineWebcams CCTV view before planning your stay in the north of the island.
/en-in/cameras/samui-choengmon/: Choeng Mon beach live webcam in north-east Samui: preview the shore, offshore water and waves through a CCTV view on the provider’s site if you are thinking of staying on this coast.
/en-in/cameras/samui-crystal-bay/: Crystal Bay Samui live webcam, also called Thongtakian Bay: watch the white sand and waves roll in on a CCTV-style YouTube stream from the yacht club before planning a seaside stay.
/en-in/cameras/samui-crystal-beach/: Silver Beach Samui live webcam: Webcamtaxi hosts this CCTV view from SamuiWebcam, listed as Crystal Bay Beach, so you can see the shoreline here before booking a stay near this bay.
/en-in/cameras/samui-two-palms/: Bang Po beach live webcam Samui: watch the waves and coast in front of Two Palms on a CCTV-style YouTube feed. Pairing the beach name with this view helps you picture the area around your hotel.
/en-in/cameras/tao-island-skyline/: Koh Tao live webcam: see the bay and islands across the sea from a beach through a SkylineWebcams CCTV view. Preview the scenery for your island trip, then pick your destination separately.
/en-in/coupons/: Thailand food app offers for Indian travellers: find official links to GrabFood Thailand on grab.com and the LINE MAN app on Google Play, so you can check current deals directly in each app.
/en-in/entry/tdac/: How to fill the Thailand TDAC arrival card on your phone: free on tdac.immigration.go.th, due within three days including arrival day. Screenshots guide you through passport, flight and hotel fields.
/en-in/entry/visa/: Thailand visa for Indians: visa-free tourism for up to 30 days from 15 September 2026, and which visa to choose for work, study or DTV. Apply via Thai e-Visa from India with Aadhaar or address proof.
/en-in/food-delivery/: Best food delivery apps in Thailand for your hotel stay: compare GrabFood, LINE MAN, ShopeeFood and Robinhood, including payment by cash or card, delivery fees and pickup from reception.
/en-in/food-delivery/grabfood/: How to order GrabFood in Thailand to your hotel: set the right map pin, choose delivery or restaurant pickup, check delivery and foreign-card fees, and keep cash ready to pay the rider if needed.
/en-in/food-delivery/line-man/: LINE MAN app Thailand food order guide: log in with a LINE ID, choose restaurants that deliver to your hotel, compare delivery and extra charges, and confirm with reception where to pick up.
/en-in/food-delivery/robinhood/: Robinhood app for food delivery in Bangkok: find restaurants that can reach your hotel, review menu prices and delivery fees before paying, and keep photos of the receipt if an item is missing.
/en-in/food-delivery/shopeefood/: ShopeeFood Thailand ordering tips: use the food menu in the Thai Shopee app, available in English, set your hotel pin, check whether a foreign card works for you, and ask reception about pickup.
/en-in/food/: Where to eat with a view in Thailand: rooftop restaurants and bars in Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Samui and Pattaya, such as Horizon at Hilton Pattaya and STAR by Silavadee, plus food delivery apps.
/en-in/rooftops/: Best rooftop bars in Thailand by city: filter 44 rooftops and viewpoints across Bangkok, Pattaya, Phuket, Chiang Mai, Samui and Phi Phi, and compare timings, age limits and booking rules.
/en-in/rooftops/abar-rooftop/: ABar Rooftop Bangkok timings and dress code: open every day from 5 pm to 1 am, casual wear allowed. A gin-focused bar at the Marriott Marquis Queen’s Park, Sukhumvit 22, for drinks after dinner.
/en-in/rooftops/above-eleven/: Above Eleven Bangkok rooftop on Sukhumvit Soi 11: try Peruvian-Japanese Nikkei dishes with city views, stay on for DJ music or Wednesday salsa, open 5 pm to 2 am daily. Book by email.
/en-in/rooftops/akara-sky-hanuman/: Hanuman Sky Bar at One City Centre, Ploenchit: a 61st-floor Bangkok rooftop themed on Hanuman from Thai mythology, open 5 pm to 2 am. Choose between the bar, observation deck and night market.
/en-in/rooftops/alfresco-64/: Alfresco 64 lebua entry rules: guests must be 20 or older and dress smart casual. This 64th-floor whisky bar at State Tower, Silom, opens 5 pm to 12:30 am with DJ sets and Bangkok views.
/en-in/rooftops/attic-by-octave/: ATTIC by Octave Bangkok: a speakeasy-style 47th-floor bar at the Marriott Sukhumvit Soi 57 serving Mexican-inspired cocktails and bites. Smart casual dress code; reservations available online.
/en-in/rooftops/baba-nest/: Baba Nest Phuket booking and minimum spend: reservation is compulsory, 1,500 baht net for hotel guests and 3,000 baht for visitors. Open 5–8 pm for sunset, it closes in rain; seats held 15 minutes.
/en-in/rooftops/baiyoke-observatory/: Baiyoke Sky tower ticket price and timings: special promotion 450 baht, open 10 am to 10 pm. After Pratunam shopping, see Bangkok from the 77th floor and the revolving 84th-floor deck.
/en-in/rooftops/barbu-pattaya/: Family rooftop restaurant in Pattaya: BARBÙ at Siam@Siam welcomes children, serving Mediterranean dishes to share on the 24th floor. The Skybar on floor 27 is adults only, so book dinner here.
/en-in/rooftops/brewski-rooftop/: Brewski Bangkok craft beer rooftop on Sukhumvit Road: open every day 5 pm to 1 am at the Radisson Blu Plaza, floors 29 and 30. Pick beers with friends and stay on from sunset to city lights.
/en-in/rooftops/char-rooftop/: CHAR rooftop bar Bangkok, Hotel Indigo on Wireless Road: enjoy live music and signature cocktails on floor 26. Tell friends to meet at the rooftop bar, not the CHAR Restaurant one floor below.
/en-in/rooftops/cities/bangkok/: Bangkok rooftop bars list with timings and entry rules: compare 30 sky bars and viewpoints, from Sky Beach and Red Sky at CentralWorld to Baiyoke Sky in Pratunam and riverside ThreeSixty.
/en-in/rooftops/cities/chiang-mai/: Chiang Mai rooftops and viewpoints: two picks with mountain views, HONG’s Sky Bar at InterContinental The Mae Ping facing Doi Suthep, and the city terrace at Wat Phra That Doi Suthep.
/en-in/rooftops/cities/pattaya/: Pattaya rooftop bars and viewpoints for families and couples: compare five picks, from kid-friendly BARBÙ and Hilton’s Horizon restaurant to the 18-plus Skybar and the Phra Tamnak Hill lookout.
/en-in/rooftops/cities/phi-phi/: Phi Phi Islands viewpoint guide: Phi Phi Don Viewpoint 2 is the hilltop lookout over the sea and island village, mapped with directions. Search for Viewpoint 2 by name, as there are several.
/en-in/rooftops/cities/phuket/: Phuket sunset bars with sea views: compare five rooftops, including Baba Nest’s infinity-pool deck, The Surface over Patong Bay, Twilight Sky at Kata and Kamala’s Vanilla Sky, with booking rules.
/en-in/rooftops/cities/samui/: Koh Samui rooftop dinner spot: STAR at Silavadee Pool Spa Resort above Lamai Bay, with tables set inside the infinity pool, Western food and cocktails. Timings and booking details on the map.
/en-in/rooftops/cocoa-xo/: Cocoa XO Bangkok timings and age limit: open 4 pm to 1 am daily at Centara Grand CentralWorld, entry 20 and above. Try handmade chocolates and cognac cocktails as a sweet stop after dinner.
/en-in/rooftops/cru-champagne-bar/: CRU Champagne Bar Bangkok for an anniversary: champagne and oysters on the 59th floor of Centara Grand CentralWorld, 5 pm to 1 am, adults 20 and above only. Arrive at sunset for city lights.
/en-in/rooftops/distil-lebua/: Distil lebua Bangkok dress code and timings: smart casual, guests 20 and above, open 5 pm to 12:30 am. Choose premium spirits, cocktails or cigars at this 64th-floor State Tower bar.
/en-in/rooftops/doi-suthep-viewpoint/: Doi Suthep temple Chiang Mai with parents: take the cable car or climb 306 naga steps, see the golden chedi and Lanna architecture, then enjoy the city view from the terrace above town.
/en-in/rooftops/flute-lebua/: Flûte lebua Bangkok rules: smart casual, children aged 7 and above allowed with an adult, open 5 pm to 12:30 am. Sip Bollinger champagne on the 64th floor with live jazz except on Mondays.
/en-in/rooftops/hongs-sky-bar/: HONG’s Sky Bar Chiang Mai booking tips: reserve on the hotel site, as tables may be cancelled if you are 15 minutes late. Smart casual, open 4 pm to midnight, with Doi Suthep views at sunset.
/en-in/rooftops/horizon-pattaya/: Horizon rooftop restaurant Hilton Pattaya for a special dinner with parents or your partner: watch the bay change colour at sunset from the 34th floor. Book a table via the Hilton dining page.
/en-in/rooftops/iris-wild-iris/: IRIS rooftop at SO/ Bangkok with Lumphini Park views: Italian dinner, aperitifs and DJ sets on floors 29–30. Timings 5 pm to midnight, till 1 am on weekends; reserve via Book Now on the site.
/en-in/rooftops/lebua-no3/: lebua No.3 Bangkok gin and vodka bar: on the 52nd floor of State Tower, Silom, open 5 pm to 12:30 am. Entry is for 20 and above with smart casual dress, so plan an adults’ evening out.
/en-in/rooftops/mahanakhon-skywalk/: Mahanakhon SkyWalk tickets and timings: 10 am to midnight, last entry 11 pm, child tickets for ages 8–12. Walk the glass floor 310 m high and the 314 m viewpoint for photos of Bangkok.
/en-in/rooftops/octave-rooftop/: Octave rooftop bar Thong Lo, Bangkok: open daily 5 pm to 2 am at the Marriott Sukhumvit 57. Arrive before sunset with friends for all-round views and stay late; smart casual dress required.
/en-in/rooftops/pastel-rooftop/: Pastel Rooftop Bangkok live music dinner on Sukhumvit Soi 11: Mediterranean food and cocktails on Aira Hotel’s 22nd floor, 5 pm to 1 am. Plan your table around the official events schedule.
/en-in/rooftops/phi-phi-viewpoint-2/: Phi Phi Don Viewpoint 2 for holiday photos: look down over the sea and village from the hill with friends who love landscape shots. It is an outdoor viewpoint, not a bar, so plan the walk up.
/en-in/rooftops/phra-tamnak-viewpoint/: Pattaya viewpoint for family photos: from Phra Tamnak Hill, capture Pattaya Beach and the city together at sunset. Going by car is easier on hot days, and book your return ride if staying after dark.
/en-in/rooftops/portrait-voyage-sky-bar/: Portrait of Voyage Sky Bar Pattaya timings: open 11:30 am to midnight at Grande Centre Point Voyage, Na Kluea. Enjoy cocktails and sea views on the 33rd floor at sunset, then the city lights.
/en-in/rooftops/red-sky-bar/: Red Sky Bar Bangkok timings: open 4 pm to 1 am daily, right above CentralWorld mall on Centara Grand’s 56th floor. Head up after shopping for cocktails, light bites and the night skyline.
/en-in/rooftops/red-sky-restaurant/: Red Sky Restaurant Bangkok for a special dinner with parents or an anniversary: steaks, seafood and European food on the 55th floor at Centara Grand CentralWorld, 5 pm to 1 am. Reserve a table.
/en-in/rooftops/seen-riverside/: SEEN Avani Riverside Bangkok: a rooftop dinner spot on floors 26–27 with indoor and outdoor seating facing the Chao Phraya River. Good for friends who enjoy DJ music with their meal in Thonburi.
/en-in/rooftops/sin-rooftop/: SIN rooftop bar Avani Riverside Bangkok timings: 5 pm to 1 am on the 27th floor. Head here for after-dinner drinks with river views; it is a different venue from SEEN restaurant downstairs.
/en-in/rooftops/sirocco/: Sirocco Bangkok dress code: men in shirts or polos with neat trousers, no sleeveless tops, sportswear or flip-flops; children welcome but must follow it too. Book online and check deposit terms.
/en-in/rooftops/sizzle-rooftop/: Sizzle rooftop Patong timings: bar 5:30 pm to 11:30 pm, restaurant 6 pm to 11 pm with last orders at 10:30. Come for sunset cocktails, then dinner with sea and forest views; reservations accepted.
/en-in/rooftops/sky-bar/: Sky Bar lebua Bangkok rules: no reservations, one drink per person, smart casual with no sleeveless tops for men, children 7 and above with an adult. Try the Hangovertini above the river.
/en-in/rooftops/sky-beach/: Sky Beach Mahanakhon Bangkok timings and entry: 10 am to midnight, last entry 11 pm, all ages welcome, no bookings as seats are first come, first served. Use the main King Power Mahanakhon entrance.
/en-in/rooftops/sky-on-20/: Sky on 20 Bangkok rooftop at Novotel Sukhumvit 20: share pizza and bruschetta with friends on the 26th floor, open 5 pm to 1 am. Visit on Friday or Saturday evening if you want DJ music.
/en-in/rooftops/skybar-summer-club/: Skybar Summer Club Pattaya age limit: entry is 18 and above, so leave kids at BARBÙ downstairs. Enjoy pools on two levels, cocktails and live DJ music with sea views after a beach day.
/en-in/rooftops/spectrum-lounge-bar/: Spectrum rooftop Bangkok dress code: smart casual, no sandals, open-toed shoes, sleeveless tops or sportswear. Dine with live music on the 29th floor, then move up for DJ sets; open 5:30 pm to 1 am.
/en-in/rooftops/spire-rooftop/: Spire rooftop Dusit Thani Bangkok with family: guests under 20 may visit until 7 pm, so come early for city views. Smart casual, no flip-flops or tank tops, open 5 pm to 1 am on Rama IV Road.
/en-in/rooftops/star-silavadee/: STAR rooftop Koh Samui for a couple’s dinner: book one of four tables set inside the infinity pool over Lamai Bay. Open 5:30 pm to 11 pm, kitchen last orders 10:30 pm; reserve online.
/en-in/rooftops/surface-patong/: The Surface rooftop Patong Beach, Phuket: after a day on the sand, go up at La Flora Resort on Taweewong Road for sunset cocktails and dinner overlooking Patong Bay with your partner or friends.
/en-in/rooftops/threesixty-rooftop/: ThreeSixty rooftop bar Millennium Hilton Bangkok timings: 5 pm to 1 am daily on Charoennakorn Road. A riverside rooftop for sunset photography and Chao Phraya views with your partner or friends.
/en-in/rooftops/tichuca-rooftop/: Tichuca rooftop bar Bangkok location: search T-ONE Building on Sukhumvit Road in Grab or Bolt, then ask staff for the 46th floor. Expect greenery, cocktails and organic house music from resident DJs.
/en-in/rooftops/twilight-sky/: Twilight Sky Kata Phuket for couples: drinks and dinner at sunset above Kata Beach at The SIS, an adults-only resort. Check the Thursday live music and steak evening and reserve by phone.
/en-in/rooftops/vanilla-sky/: Vanilla Sky Kamala Phuket sunset bar timings: 5 pm to midnight at Cape Sienna hotel. Enjoy charcoal-grilled food and cocktails facing Kamala Bay, and email ahead for a reservation.
/en-in/rooftops/yao-rooftop/: Yao rooftop bar Bangkok for non-drinkers too: alcohol-free drinks are served alongside cocktails and dim sum at the Marriott Surawongse. Open 5 pm to 1 am, casual dress, reservations by phone.

/en-in/travel-seasons/bangkok/: Best time to visit Bangkok is November to February, when rain drops sharply and December–January average about 27°C. See month-wise temperature and rainfall, with tips to beat the April heat.
/en-in/travel-seasons/chiang-mai/: Best time to visit Chiang Mai is November to January, averaging 22–25°C with little rain and cool mornings, so pack a light layer. Month-wise rainfall and temperatures help you plan temple days.
/en-in/travel-seasons/koh-samui/: Best time to visit Koh Samui is February to April. Unlike Phuket and Krabi, Samui’s heavy rain falls in October–December, peaking at 444.6mm in November, while February is driest at 64.3mm.
/en-in/travel-seasons/krabi/: Best time to visit Krabi is December to March for beaches and limestone cliffs, with February driest at 35.9mm. See month-wise rain and heat, and plan boat trips around daily operating notices.
/en-in/travel-seasons/pattaya/: Best time to visit Pattaya is November to February, when December and January see just 11.7mm and 16.3mm of rain. Month-by-month temperatures and rainfall help you plan beach walks and time in town.
/en-in/travel-seasons/phuket/: Best time to visit Phuket is December to March, with February driest at 24.0mm and highs near 34°C by March. Compare month-wise rain from May to November and how wind and waves affect boat tours.
